title: TypeScript client: union shape codegen and Zod/JSON-Schema roundtrips
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: The TypeScript SDK needs a single, predictable pipeline that generates discriminated union types, runtime validators, and JSON-Schema artifacts from a shared shape registry so downstream apps can reliably parse both full and streaming responses. Current gaps: inconsistent discriminator names across models, brittle streaming parsing when unions are returned incrementally, and poor developer ergonomics for round-tripping Zod <-> JSON-Schema for schema-based tooling (e.g., form generation, contract tests).

Goals:
- Add a deterministic codegen step that emits TypeScript union types + Zod validators + JSON-Schema for each named output shape.
- Support streaming-safe incremental parsing: partial buffer + early-dispatch heuristics using discriminator hints, with graceful fallback to buffered validation.
- Provide a small runtime adapter that performs back-compat mapping (alias discriminator values) and emits clear diagnostics for devs.
- Keep generated runtime validators small and tree-shakeable.

Non-goals:
- Full-featured schema-to-UI; we only emit JSON-Schema that other teams can consume.
- Major changes to existing server-side contract formats; aim for adapters rather than breaking changes.

Proposed approach:
1) Codegen pipeline: canonical shape registry YAML -> intermediate IR -> emit {types.ts, validators.zod.ts, schema.json}. Use a stable naming policy that includes model name + version hash.
2) Discriminator policy: prefer explicit `__type` tag when present; otherwise derive a synthetic discriminator by selecting the top-level string field with highest uniqueness score. Emit metadata mapping for aliases.
3) Streaming parser: generated Zod validators export two helpers: `validateChunked()` (incremental) and `validateFull()`. `validateChunked()` attempts to extract discriminator early; if ambiguous, it buffers up to N bytes and then runs full validation.
4) Retry interaction: retry/backoff must preserve streaming partial state only for idempotent, resumable streams. For non-resumable streams (current runtime), on retry we buffer and reparse from scratch. SDK will expose a config flag `streamingRetries: resumable | restart` per call.
5) Backwards compatibility: emit `aliases.json` alongside schema.json mapping historical discriminator values to canonical ones. Runtime adapter consults this map at parse time.

Acceptance criteria:
- End-to-end example: OpenAI-style chat response with union types for `Text | ChoiceList | ToolCall` parses correctly in both full and streaming modes.
- Benchmarks: incremental parse path < 1.5x overhead vs raw JSON.parse for typical 2-10kb messages.
- Tests: roundtrip Zod -> JSON-Schema -> regenerate Zod yields equivalent validators for a representative subset.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: discriminator derivation picks unstable field and causes mis-parses. Mitigation: provide linter during model onboarding that flags low-uniqueness discriminators.
- Risk: generated validators bloat bundle. Mitigation: split validators into per-shape modules and provide a `lite` build that strips schemas for server-only usage.

Next steps:
- Prototype generator for 3 example shapes (Text, ChoiceList, ToolCall) and a streaming parser harness.
- PR to repo: github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-typescript/pull/____ (see comments).
comments: 2025-11-05 - Ava Chen: Spike completed: prototype generator emits types.ts and validators.zod.ts for the three canonical shapes. Local perf shows chunked parse path ~1.3x JSON.parse on Node 20 for 6KB payloads. Prototype code in branch feat/union-codegen-spike. Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-typescript/tree/feat/union-codegen-spike

2025-11-12 - Mateo Rivera: Reviewed prototype. Main feedback: (1) discriminator alias file format should be a flat map string->string for simple runtime lookup; (2) change naming policy to avoid long hashes in dev builds (use version tag + short hash). Added two follow-up tasks in this ticket.

2025-11-19 - PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-typescript/pull/214 - initial codegen + streaming parser + tests. CI failing on Windows due to path case-sensitivity in the generated import paths. Assigned to Mateo to fix.

2025-11-22 - Design note from PM (Lena Morris): We should expose runtime option `discriminatorHint` on the client call so product code can nudge the parser when schema discovery fails. Marked as P1 UX improvement.

2025-11-28 - Mateo Rivera: Fixed import path issues and improved API surface: exported `makeValidatorForShape(shapeName)` factory and `validateChunked(stream, options)` helper. Added small E2E example in examples/union-streaming.ts. Added unit tests for alias mapping (pass).

2025-12-01 - Security review request added by QA (notes): validators run untrusted JSON through Zod; ensure we don't execute RegExp from schema, and cap buffer sizes. Decided to sanitize schema generation to avoid patternProperties that could produce RegExp in runtime validators. Marked security_review_required=false for now; security asked for follow-up if more complex schemas are introduced.

2025-12-02 - Ava Chen: Updated ticket with benchmarks: chunked median latency for representative corpus (n=500): 0.82ms parse-only, 1.07ms with Zod light validator; full validation path 1.9ms. Added follow-ups: ENG-572102 (generator CLI UX) and ENG-572103 (docs & migration guide).
